title: Survival Analysis via Density Estimation
summary: Theorem 5.3 fails without identifiability even for a smooth fixed copula and positive marginal densities. Appendix D.2 also substitutes integrated-in-covariate error for a pointwise conditional bound and uses an incorrect Hellinger/L1 inequality.
limitations: No author code execution, empirical reruns or historical-code attribution.
Full Proposition C.3 induction and imported estimator theorems not independently certified.
No comprehensive later-version or errata search.

problems.title: NLL-SC strict propriety requires an identifiable latent model class

source_claim.paraphrase: Finite observable-law KL suffices for equality of expected scores only at true latent marginal CDFs.

assumptions: Known copula density c(u,v)=h((v-u) mod1), h(z)=6sin^2(3pi z) on (1/3,2/3), else0
c nonnegative with uniform margins; copula C2, absolutely continuous, no ties
Candidate F2=t; F1=t for t<=2/3, else t+s^2(1-s)^2/3, s=3t-2
Same known copula for both models; both observed cause probabilities1/2
problems.check: No copula mass occurs where u,v>2/3. Models agree below 2/3 and are unobservable above it. Each observable cause subdensity equals 1 for t<=1/3, then 2-3t+sin(6pi t)/(2pi), then0. It integrates to1/2. Latent F1 differs by1/48 at5/6.
problems.result: Identical observable distribution and expected NLL-SC, but distinct latent marginals.
counterevidence: Counterexample violates the positive lower copula-density condition of Assumption C.1; it does not refute Theorem C.2.
No claim of nonidentifiability for the paper's specific independence/Frank experimental setting.
The KL proof remains valid for observable laws.
problems.core_dependency: Strict propriety for competing risks and associated SC-Net latent-target guarantee are named central contributions.
problems.impact: Universal latent strict-propriety theorem is false under stated assumptions; experimental scores need not change.

correction.statement: NLL-SC is strictly proper for the observable law; strict propriety for latent marginals additionally requires injectivity of the fixed-copula observation map on the admissible class.

problems.title: Integrated density error does not imply a pointwise conditional cell bound

source_claim.location: Appendix D.2 p.25, final paragraphs; target Eq.18 p.14
source_claim.paraphrase: An integrated Hellinger/TV guarantee implies Eq.18 at x by taking epsilon equal to global TV.

assumptions: On a centered feature interval A_eta of mass eta, estimator q=(23/40,7/40,1/8,1/8); elsewhere estimator equals r
Both densities positive and normalized; histogram representation valid
problems.check: Integrated unhalved L1=2eta/5; at fixed x=1/2 cell error=1/5. With eta=1/100, claimed epsilon1/250 is smaller than actual1/5. As eta shrinks, integrated error tends0 but fixed-x error remains. At eta1, L1=.4 versus displayed squared Hellinger .05894368065 (root .2427831968).
problems.result: Both stated norm inequality and pointwise conditional inference fail.
counterevidence: Does not refute cited Sart oracle theorem or show a particular fitted estimator necessarily yields this error sequence.
An independent uniform conditional accuracy guarantee could still supply Theorem C.2's premise.
A factor correction alone does not solve the covariate quantifier change.
problems.core_dependency: Appendix D.2 provides the claimed route from a general density estimator to the conditional accuracy premise of the main reduction/convergence contribution.
problems.impact: Invalidates this route to Eq.18; conditional Step2 theorem and separate DRF route are not refuted.

correction.statement: For normalized densities L1<=2H, where H is root Hellinger. Integrated error bounds expected error or bad-X probability; it does not by itself provide uniform conditional control.
